name: watering-pot-charming

purpose.why: Rebuilt on Evan's request (2026-10-22) to replace the Ranch tile's original model with a crafted one, keeping its game role.
purpose.audience: children building and playing in a miniature ranch

brief.prompt: a whimsical storybook version of a round glazed terracotta watering pot with a long spout and a curved handle, chunky rounded toy-like proportions, a playful little tilt

concept.tool: Midjourney web app (midjourney.com/imagine), driven in Evan's signed-in Chrome by Claude through the Claude in Chrome extension, one job at a time, text prompts only (no image reference)

hero.prompt: a whimsical storybook version of a round glazed terracotta watering pot with a long spout and a curved handle, chunky rounded toy-like proportions, a playful little tilt, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 1:1
hero.pick_reason: glossy glazed terracotta, long spout and curved handle, round body; variant 2 was a blue teapot

construction.by: modeler agent, directed by the art director (Claude)

rounds.change: Normal build reshaped from hero pixel measurements: flat-based ellipsoid belly, two-band collar, short fat spout with rolled mouth, ear handle, 4 deg lean. Camera at 90/10.
Camera fixed at 85/5 after a calibration grid; smooth shading, less wobble, wider base, belly a little lower.
Belly centre lowered, spout root fatter and lower, handle pulled in and thickened, tapering fatter at the joins.
Tried a pear-shaped belly (0.920, dropped); kept a lower handle arch.
Belly rings sampled evenly by angle and crease splitting at 38 deg, so the collar reads as a separate fat ring on a round belly (as in the hero) instead of a conical shoulder.
Belly made a sunk sphere meeting the ground on a 0.072 m disc (no foot ring, like the hero). A z-squash sweep gave only noise, kept 1.0.
Spout root lowered 6 mm and fattened.
Final 768 px / 48 sample render and hero score; to_game.py watering-pot-charming.

what_was_done: Copied build.py, make_views.py, hero_check.py and run.sh from models/watering-pot/ and reshaped the same three-part design (pot_body lathe, spout tube, handle tube), the same Clay_Glaze material, origin at the centre of the base on the ground, spout to -Y, no variants (garden prop).

Hero only (no turnaround was made for this prop). views/hero.png is the MJ hero keyed by hue (make_views.py): pot hue < 0.068 with saturation > 0.10 kept, so the pale specular highlights stay in; the browner cast shadow to the left (hue 0.075 to 0.09) and the cream backdrop are dropped; small enclosed holes are filled and the handle loop is left open.

The hero is a near side view from +X, a little above (the open top shows as a thin ellipse, about 8 deg). A yaw/elevation grid on the round-1 model preferred 80/0 (0.929), but that partly compensates for shape errors, so I fixed it at 85 deg yaw, 5 deg up as a compromise with what the image shows and held it there for every round.

An 18-segment lathe: a big ellipsoid belly (r 0.133 m, centre 0.106 m, vertical radius 0.128 m) sunk into the ground so it meets it on a 0.072 m flat disc with no foot ring, sampled evenly by angle up to a short neck, then a fat collar: a lower band, a groove, and a thick rolled lip (r 0.081 m) round a wide open top with an inside wall and floor.
A 10-sided tube, shorter and much fatter than the normal pot's: it leaves the upper belly with a 0.05 m root, rises at about 47 deg and ends 0.28 m up in a big rolled mouth (r 0.025 m).

A chunky ear handle (r 0.0165 m, swelling to 0.02 m at both joins) from the back of the lip, over a tight round loop and down into the back of the belly, instead of the normal pot's tall thin arch over the top.

Smooth shading with crisp creases (lathe edges sharper than 38 deg are split, so the collar bands and lip stay crisp), a glossier glaze (roughness 0.40), a 4 deg sideways lean (a shear with height, so the base still sits flat), and much lower vertex wobble.

1,438 triangles (budget 2k), 3 meshes, one material Clay_Glaze (role clay), flat base colour, no textures, exported with export_animations=False. 0.31 m tall, 0.40 m long spout tip to handle back, 0.26 m wide. to_game.py watering-pot-charming installed it as garden-assets-charming/GF-074.glb.
construction.creative_additions: A crisp groove between the collar's two bands, a thick rolled mouth on the spout, handle joins that swell like pinched clay, and a small sideways lean.

geometry.up: Z (Blender source); Y in GLB and game
geometry.origin: centre of the footprint, on the ground

good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.938 at 768 px / 48 samples from the hero's direction: round belly, collar, spout with its rolled mouth and the ear handle all line up.
Reads at tile size as the same round orange watering pot, just chubbier: same spout-left, handle-right silhouette, same colour and material role.
off: Footprint ratio: 0.40 m long by 0.26 m wide (1.52:1) against the normal pot's 0.45 by 0.24 (1.86:1). The hero's spout is short and the belly fat, and the game scales props to a set height, so at equal height the charming pot is the same length as the normal one but about 25 % wider. I followed the hero rather than stretching it.
The hero's spout blends into the belly with a soft fillet; mine is a fat tube pushed into the belly.
The hero's glaze has painted highlights; mine is one flat colour (the glossier roughness carries some of that).
The lean is my addition from the prompt's 'playful little tilt'; the hero itself stands nearly upright, so I kept it to 4 deg and sideways, where it barely touches the hero silhouette.
Round-to-round IoU differences under about 0.01 are render noise at 384 px (a z-scale sweep jumped around by that much), so the later rounds were judged by eye as much as by number.
